speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has carried out inspections on licensed caterers providing food for migrant workers to ensure that food is prepared within four hours of the workers' lunch and dinner times; (b) if not, whether SFA will consider carrying out such inspections; and (c) if yes, how many inspections are carried out in 2023 and 2024.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think we know that many of the workers have their lunch at about noon.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That means the food can be prepared, the earliest time is 8.00 am.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we also know that by 8.00 am, many of these workers are already at the worksite or on the way to the worksite.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is not even counting the time it takes to deliver the food.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is not really an issue of when the food is prepared or when the caterer delivers the food.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But it is the coordination between the timing of when the food needs to be consumed, which is between the operator on the ground and the workers or the company.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is something that the company needs to communicate to the caterer about, on when they want the food delivered.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Otherwise, the kitchen would not know when the worker is going to consume the food.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is a rule from SFA that the food should be consumed within four hours.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In fact, I know that many of the food is actually prepared at about 4.00 am.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, by the time it is delivered and when the workers are on the lorry, actually the food has already passed the four-hour mark.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, it is our rule and I am just wondering whether SFA can now work with MOM to make sure that this rule is actually enforced.
